issues.display_title: Issue #446: Editor save downgrades a published project to draft
issues.main_description_html:
The dashboard's "Published" status flips to "Draft" after editing a project. Every editor save (manual and autosave) sends updateProject(id, { canvasData, status: "edited" }) unconditionally (EditorTopbar.saveNow), overwriting a published status; the dashboard shows anything ≠ published as "Draft".

Fix

  • Keep the project's status in the map store when the editor loads the project (useWizardPersistence — the single project-load path).
  • In saveNow, only send status: "edited" when the current status is not published.

Acceptance criteria

  • Saving/autosaving a published project keeps it "Published" on the dashboard.
  • Saving a non-published project still moves it to edited.
  • BE counterpart guards the transition server-side (see BE task).

Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer
Parent feedback: #439

RESULT

Root cause: EditorTopbar.saveNow sent status: "edited" on every save (manual + autosave), downgrading a published project; the dashboard shows anything ≠ published as "Draft".

Fix: the map store now keeps the backend project status (projectStatus in projectSlice), set where the editor loads the project payload (useWizardPersistence). saveNow omits the status field when the current status is published — publish state only changes via the publish/unpublish endpoints. Non-published projects still move to edited on save.

BE counterpart: Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#119 guards the same transition server-side.

issues.display_title: Issue #454: Empty project: .txt import leaves the No-floors card and never saves
issues.main_description_html:
Repro

  1. Open an empty project (no floors) in the editor.
  2. Import a floorplan .txt via the "No floors yet" card's dropzone (drop or browse), e.g. the edited_floorplan (4).txt attached to #439.
  3. The walls render on the canvas (and in the 3D view), but:
    • the "No floors yet" card stays on top of the canvas, and
    • nothing is ever saved — reloading the project shows an empty project again.

Cause
EmptyProjectPlaceholder.loadTxt only calls engine.loadText(text, name). The model lands in the floorplan engine, but no floor is created in the store: floorConfigs and canvasData.levels stay empty, so

  • hasFloors(floorConfigs, canvasData) stays false → EditorCanvas keeps rendering the placeholder, and
  • the engine→store sync has no level to write into, so autosave persists nothing.

Fix direction
Importing a .txt on an empty project must first create a floor (floor config + canvasData level, same as Add Floor), then load the model into it — so the placeholder hides and the engine sync/autosave has a level target.

Acceptance criteria

  • Importing a .txt on an empty project hides the "No floors yet" card and shows the imported floorplan.
  • A floor exists afterwards (floor list shows it) and the project autosaves — reload shows the imported floorplan.
  • Add Floor flow unchanged.

Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer
Parent feedback: #439 (attachment file)

RESULT

Root cause confirmed as scoped: EmptyProjectPlaceholder.loadTxt called engine.loadText only — the model landed in the engine, but no floor existed in the store, so hasFloors() stayed false (card stayed up) and the engine→store sync had no level to persist (no autosave).

Fix: the dropzone now goes through the store instead of the engine — parse via the existing txtToLevel, add a floor config (Floor N, height 3, originalFileName = the imported file), append the level to canvasData (adopting computeCoordSpace when the project had none) and set it active. FloorplanEditor's level-load effect then loads the model into the engine, the card unmounts (hasFloors true), and setCanvasData marks unsaved so autosave persists it. A malformed .txt shows a red error line under the dropzone instead of silently doing nothing.

issues.display_title: Issue #455: Add Floor import: MapThru floorplan .txt is sent to the Mappedin JSON endpoint
issues.main_description_html:
Repro
Add Floor modal → Import → pick a MapThru floorplan .txt export (e.g. edited_floorplan (5).txt attached to #447) → red error: invalid editor export JSON: invalid character '2' after top-level value.

Cause
useAddLevel.handleImport sends every .txt/.json to /api/import/mappedin-editor, which parses a Mappedin editor export (JSON). A MapThru floorplan .txt is the engine's own plain-number format (W H / wall count / coordinate lines) — the Go JSON decoder reads the first number as a top-level value and fails on the second.

Fix

  • Sniff the file content in handleImport: if it does not start with {/[, treat it as a MapThru floorplan .txt and convert locally via txtToLevel (modal name + height apply) — same path the empty-project dropzone uses since #454. JSON still goes to /api/import/mappedin-editor, .zip to /api/import/mappedin.
  • Extract the shared "append floorplan txt as a new floor" logic (floor config + level + coordSpace + active level) into lib/editor/levels.ts and reuse it from both the dropzone and the modal.

Acceptance criteria

  • Importing a MapThru floorplan .txt from the Add Floor modal creates the floor and shows it (no BE call, no error).
  • A malformed .txt shows the modal's error state.
  • Mappedin editor JSON and .zip imports unchanged.

Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer
Parent feedback: #447

RESULT

handleImport now sniffs the file content before choosing a route: a .txt that does not start with {/[ is a MapThru floorplan export (plain numbers) and is converted locally via the new appendTxtLevel helper — floor config uses the modal's name + height, the level is appended with a computed coordSpace when the building had none, and the floor becomes active. Mappedin editor JSON still goes to /api/import/mappedin-editor and .zip to /api/import/mappedin; no BE change. A malformed .txt shows the modal's error state instead of the Go JSON error.

Shared logic extracted to lib/editor/levels.ts (isFloorplanTxt + appendTxtLevel) and the empty-project dropzone (#454) now reuses it. 5 unit tests added (format sniffing, parse/append/coordSpace, throw on non-floorplan text).

issues.display_title: Issue #468: Map markers: per-frame display churn forces full reflow every frame on dense projects
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

The editor Map view (and preview/live, same component) stutters on marker-dense projects — reported on project 43fada28 (262 objects, heavy pano-chip overlap): visible lag while panning/rotating the map.

Root cause

MapObjectMarkers's per-frame reposition() uses style.display to cull off-screen markers (pass 1) and hide decluttered markers (pass 3), then reads offsetWidth/offsetHeight of every on-screen marker (pass 2). With overlapping markers the declutter pass flips display: none ↔ "" on the same buttons every frame, so layout is invalidated every frame and pass 2 forces a full reflow every frame.

Measured in-situ on the reported project (128 markers in DOM): size reads cost 0.4 ms with clean layout vs 9.2 ms with the display churn — more than half the 16 ms frame budget burned on reflow before MapLibre/three.js even render. CPU profile during a drag: reposition ≈ 5.3 s self-time.

Fix

  • Switch the initial style and all three reposition() write sites from display to visibility.
  • Write only when the value actually changes.

visibility does not affect layout, so layout stays clean and the per-frame size reads become free. visibility: hidden elements are still unclickable and invisible (same behavior) and remain measurable (display: none reports 0×0), which is also more correct for declutter.

Acceptance criteria

  • No forced reflow per frame from reposition() (size-read cost back to ~0.4 ms)
  • Culled/decluttered markers still hidden and non-interactive
  • Marker drag, hover bubbles, dot mode, declutter behavior unchanged

Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

RESULT

Switched marker hide/show in MapObjectMarkers from style.display to style.visibility (initial JSX style + all three reposition() write sites), with a change-guard so unchanged frames write nothing. Layout is never dirtied by the per-frame loop, so pass 2's offsetWidth/offsetHeight reads no longer force a reflow. Hidden markers stay non-interactive and invisible, and remain measurable (more correct for declutter than display:none's 0×0).

Measured on the reported project (43fada28, 262 objects / 128 markers in DOM):

issues.display_title: Issue #471: Wizard: retried floor scan appends its level out of order in rebuildTwin
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

StepGenerate.rebuildTwin builds canvasData.levels from resultsRef Map insertion order. The first generation pass is sequential so order matches floorConfigs — but a floor that FAILED on the first pass is absent from the map, and when retried (Retry Failed / row Retry) its first set() appends it at the END. Result: canvasData.levels = completion order (e.g. [1,3,4,2]) while floorConfigs stays [1,2,3,4]. This is the likely original corruption behind #469 — the mismatch persists into every viewer.

Fix

Order the merge by floorConfigs, not map insertion:

const entries = floorConfigs
  .map((c) => [c.id, resultsRef.current.get(c.id)] as const)
  .filter((e): e is [string, ScanResult] => !!e[1]);

Acceptance criteria

  • A floor that fails then succeeds on retry lands at its floorConfigs position in canvasData.levels
  • Twin levels order matches too (same entries feed mergeResults)

Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

RESULT

rebuildTwin in StepGenerate.tsx now assembles its entries by iterating floorConfigs and looking results up in the map, instead of spreading the results Map's insertion order. A floor that fails the first pass and succeeds on Retry now lands at its floorConfigs position in both canvasData.levels and the Digital Twin's levels (same entries feed mergeResults), instead of being appended after later floors — the likely original corruption behind #469.

Context

The 3D floormap will be embedded on tourmkr.com as a minimap with two-way panorama sync (tour changes pano → floormap selects the matching point; floormap marker click → tour moves to that pano). The bridge already exists and works (src/lib/preview/tourBridge.ts + src/lib/preview/tourSync.ts + src/components/editor/preview/useTourSync.ts, wired into /embed/[key] via PreviewOverlay), but it speaks a custom contract (select-panorama / panorama-changed). tourmkr already speaks the gothru-maps contract — the floormap must use exactly the same message types.

Reference implementation (gothru-maps-frontend):

  • Inbound src/components/main/maps/container/main/PostMessage.tsx — { type: "PANO_CHANGE", data: <panoId> } (data is the bare pano id) and { type: "ANGLE_CHANGE", data: <degrees> }
  • Outbound src/helpers/postMessage.ts + ModerationMapEvents.tsx — window.parent.postMessage({ type: "PANO_CHANGE", data: { panoId: Number(panoId), tourKey } }, ...) on marker click

Description

Change the message contract in src/lib/preview/tourBridge.ts (and its consumers/tests) to match gothru-maps exactly:

  • Inbound (tour → floormap): accept { type: "PANO_CHANGE", data: <panoId> } — bare id in data, tolerate number or string — and apply it as the current panorama-changed path does (match marker by panorama id → set active + center). Drop the { source: "gothru", type: "panorama-changed" } shape.
  • Outbound (floormap → tour): on marker selection post { type: "PANO_CHANGE", data: { panoId, tourKey } } instead of { source: "mapthru", type: "select-panorama" }. panoId numeric like the reference; tourKey from the imported tour if available (flag it in the PR if the embed context has no tour key to send).
  • Keep the LoopGuard — the type is now identical in both directions, so echo suppression matters more, not less.
  • Fix the origin allowlist while touching the bridge: GOTHRU_TOUR_ORIGINS only has https://tourmkr.com and https://gothru.co. gothru-maps also allows https://www.tourmkr.com, https://tourmkr.app, https://www.tourmkr.app, https://www.gothru.co — mirror that list, otherwise embeds on the www domain silently drop every message. Also correct the misleading comment in useTourSync.ts claiming the referrer origin is accepted at runtime (it is only used as targetOrigin).

ANGLE_CHANGE (camera direction) is out of scope here — separate task if the minimap needs a direction indicator.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Inbound { type: "PANO_CHANGE", data: <panoId> } (number or string) from an allowed origin selects + centers the matching marker in /embed/[key]
  • Floormap marker selection posts { type: "PANO_CHANGE", data: { panoId, tourKey } } to the parent window
  • No select-panorama / panorama-changed shapes remain
  • Loop guard still prevents ping-pong (tour echoing our own PANO_CHANGE back is a no-op)
  • Origin allowlist covers tourmkr.com/tourmkr.app/gothru.co incl. www variants; unknown origins still rejected
  • Unit tests in src/lib/preview/__tests__/ updated to the new shapes
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Bridge contract replaced with gothru-maps' exactly (commit cfd11d9, branch feature/503-align-embed-postmessage):

  • Outbound { type: "PANO_CHANGE", data: { panoId: number, tourKey } } on marker selection; tourKey resolved from Information.pano.tourKey (empty string when absent).
  • select-panorama / panorama-changed shapes removed entirely.
  • LoopGuard kept — echo of our own selection is swallowed.
  • Origin allowlist widened to www.tourmkr.com, tourmkr.app, www.tourmkr.app, www.gothru.co (+ existing tourmkr.com, gothru.co); misleading referrer comment in useTourSync.ts corrected (referrer only picks targetOrigin, never joins the allowlist).

Follow-up (commit 00d59b5)

Two embed-sync fixes from testing against the tour player:

  • Info card was only hidden on /embed/[key]; a GoThru tour iframing the live /v/[key] url still showed it. Added isGothruTourReferrer() — the card now also hides when iframed with a GoThru tour referrer; other sites iframing the live view keep it.
